knowledge-base.name: consult-mode
knowledge-base.triggers: consult mode, auto mode, architectural decision, collaborative, propose before coding, ask before implementing, free roam, task plan, vision check
knowledge-base.overview: ClaudeBoost CONSULT/AUTO mode protocol. CONSULT is the default — before starting any task that builds or changes something, Claude describes what it's about to create in plain language and waits for the user to confirm the vision. Once confirmed, Claude grinds freely without asking again. AUTO is a bypass for prototyping and trivial work.

session-approvals.purpose: Remember architectural choices the user approved earlier in this session so Claude does not re-consult on the same axis
session-approvals.lifecycle: Cleared at SessionStart. Written by main agent after each AskUserQuestion approval. Read before every architectural-decision classification.

vision-check-trigger.overview: CONSULT protocol fires at the START of any task that creates new things or makes choices that affect what the user will see or experience. One check per task, not per file. The gate is a speed bump at task start, not a tollbooth on every edit.

fires-when.condition: Any request to build, implement, add, or create something — a feature, page, component, service, command, config, workflow
Any architectural choice where different approaches produce meaningfully different user-visible outcomes (e.g. JWT with refresh tokens vs single short-lived token)
Resuming work after context compaction if no task-plan.json exists for the current session

does-not-fire.condition: Grinding through an approved task — edits, file writes, and sub-steps within a task already confirmed by task-plan.json
Bugfixes, typos, formatting, test-only changes, doc edits, renames within a single file
/self-improve — runs in AUTO context, no gate
Changes under workspace/, knowledge/, plans/, docs/ — low-stakes meta files

consultation-protocol.overview: Task-level vision check. One check before work starts, then grind freely. This is Devin's pattern: plain-language plan → user approval → execute start to finish.
consultation-protocol.step:
Before writing any file, output 2-3 sentences describing: 1. What the result will look/work like from the USER's perspective (not technical spec) 2. Any meaningful choice where different approaches produce different outcomes the user would care about
Format: plain English, concrete, specific. Say what the user will see or experience.
Good: "I'm going to build a yellow bird that flies through green pipes. There's a score counter at the top. I'll use a canvas element — if you want sound effects I can add those too." Bad: "I'll implement a Canvas-based 2D physics engine with requestAnimationFrame loop and collision detection..."
Stop after the vision check. Do not write code, do not write files. Wait for the user's response.

The user will: - Confirm as-is ("yes", "looks good", "go") - Adjust the vision ("make it purple instead of green", "add a timer") - Redirect entirely ("actually I want a side-scroller, not flappy bird")
Do NOT start implementing until the user responds. The consult-gate.py hook will surface a permission dialog if you try to create a new file without a logged plan.

After user confirms, write state/task-plan.json: { "task": "plain-language summary of what was agreed (≤2 sentences)", "approved_at": "YYYY-MM-DD", "scope_hint": "optional: files or area this covers" } Overwrite any previous task-plan.json — this records the current task's approval.

Grind freely. No more gates until the next new task. RAG-required standards (parameterized queries, logger.error in catch, input validation, auth checks) apply automatically throughout — they were never up for debate.

additive-not-gatekeeping.principle: CONSULT mode is NOT asking "may I do this?" — it is announcing "here is what I am about to do, so you can add constraints I should layer on."
additive-not-gatekeeping.rag-required: RAG-sourced standards are applied without consultation: SQL parameterization, logger.error in catch blocks, input validation at boundaries, auth checks on endpoints, no secrets in logs. These are not options — they always happen.
additive-not-gatekeeping.user-layer: User's role in consultation is to ADD constraints: size caps, character allowlists, rate limits, retry budgets, timeout values, acceptable input formats, error message wording, observability hooks. Claude's proposal names the defaults; user refines.
additive-not-gatekeeping.example: Feature: "add file upload endpoint" Vision check: "Users will be able to upload files to their profile. I'll accept any file type and store it in S3 — if you want a size limit or file type restriction, say so now." User adds: "10MB max, only .png/.jpg/.pdf, reject non-ASCII filenames." Claude logs to task-plan.json and implements both what was planned and the user's add-ons, including the non-negotiable standards layer automatically.

task-plan-state.purpose: Records that a task vision has been confirmed by the user. The consult-gate.py hook reads this to decide whether to escalate a new-file Write to a permission dialog.
task-plan-state.lifecycle: Written after user approves a task vision. Overwritten when a new task starts. Cleared at session end (not persisted across sessions — task-plan.json is session-scoped).
task-plan-state.hook-reads-this: consult-gate.py: if task-plan.json exists → pass silently; if not → permissionDecision:"ask"

auto-mode.behavior: Claude proceeds autonomously on architectural decisions but still cites patterns it follows. No architect-agent spawn. No AskUserQuestion.
auto-mode.when-to-use: Prototyping, exploration, trivial work where the user has said "just do it". Rework cost is low.
auto-mode.when-not-to-use: Production code, security-sensitive areas, cross-cutting concerns, anything the user might want to see first.

slash-commands.command: Switch to AUTO mode. Bypass consultation.

hook.purpose: Load CONSULT protocol into every session's context via session-primer.py
consult-gate.py: if CONSULT mode + new file + no task-plan.json → permissionDecision:ask. Passes silently for existing files (grinding) and all Edit/Bash calls.
Re-inject CONSULT/AUTO rule after context compaction
